did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hoshea son of Elah was the last king of Israel. He reigned in Samaria for nine years, beginning in the twelfth year of the reign of Ahaz king of Judah.
Did you know? Hoshea rebelled against the king of Assyria by refusing to pay him tribute and sending messengers to So king of Egypt. As a result, the king of Assyria arrested and imprisoned him.
Did you know? After conquering Samaria, the king of Assyria exiled the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, along the Habor River at Gozan, and in the cities of Media.
Did you know? The chapter explains Israel’s exile as the result of sin against the LORD, who had brought them out of Egypt, including the worship of other gods.
Did you know? According to the chapter, the LORD warned Israel and Judah through the prophets and seers to turn from their evil ways and keep his commandments.
Did you know? The sins of Israel mentioned in the chapter include making two cast-metal calves, worshiping Baal, worshiping the host of heaven, and setting up an Asherah pole.
Did you know? The chapter also describes sacrificing sons and daughters in the fire, along with practicing sorcery and divination, as acts that provoked the LORD to anger.
Did you know? The account also connects Israel’s exile with the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel away from worshiping the LORD and led them into the sin of worshiping the calves.
Did you know? After the exile of Israel, the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the Israelites.

Did you know? The new inhabitants of Samaria feared the LORD but continued to worship their own gods and idols as well. Thus, a mixed form of worship developed that did not conform to Israel’s covenant with the LORD.
